label: Counterfactual guidance by an outweighed reason: it would prevail where not outweighed
term: counterfactual guidance by an outweighed reason (GuidedByOutweighed)
definition: GuidedByOutweighed rk good ctrl φ s r x y: the reason for y in respect r is outweighed at s (DEF 35ab5a34-4c6a-4327-97a2-a739a4263257), and in some scenario t that agrees with s on the control ctrl and keeps respect r's ranking of y over x, the profile favours y over x. It is a counterfactual, profile-level property: it says the reason not acted on at s makes a difference where it is not outweighed, not that the source's actual state registers it. Example: an agent who passes over the kinder plan only because the other is fairer, and takes it when fairness is equal. Non-example: a favouring fixed to x in every scenario.
note: Stipulative analyst notion (#2145 premise lane C, round 3), attribution deferred. See docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md, section 'Counterfactual guidance and self-application against imitability exemplars'. Registration of the outweighed reason in the actual state is a separate, realization-level question (degreeOnlyRegistersNoRespectBetweenTies).
